sections.title: Start here: a directory of buyers, not a buyer
sections.read: Three layers sit behind the one name, and only the bottom one places equipment orders.
ps: **The firm.** BlackRock, Inc. is a manager. It invests other people's money for a fee and signs no purchase order for a battery, a switchgear line-up or a turbine.

**The funds.** Its Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) funds, and a partnership it chairs called the AI Infrastructure Partnership (AIP), own or co-own companies: data-centre landlords, a utility, renewables sponsors and battery owners.
**The platforms.** Those companies — Aligned, CyrusOne, ALLETE, Eolian and others — employ the engineers who write specifications and sign the orders.

This guide teaches the machinery that connects the three layers: passive against controlling ownership, joint control, utility take-private approvals, off-balance-sheet campuses and the ladder every deal climbs. It ends with the test that matters to a seller: through which platforms does an investor actually buy?

sections.title: Index funds: owning a lot without deciding anything
sections.read: Why BlackRock can hold 11% of a utility and still have no say over its purchasing.
ps: An {{index fund}} buys every company in a published index in proportion to its weight — mostly by market value — instead of picking stocks. An {{ETF}} is a fund whose shares trade on an exchange like a company's; most track an index.

Run at a scale of trillions of dollars, following an index means owning a large slice of every big company. The PJM market monitor lists BlackRock's passive stakes in 2026 as Exelon 11.02%, PSEG 10.41%, Talen 9.01%, NextEra 8.58%, FirstEnergy 8.49% and NRG 8.48%.

US law separates such holders from controllers. A holder above 5% who certifies it is passive files a short {{Schedule 13G}}; one who can or will influence control files a {{Schedule 13D}}. BlackRock's index stakes are on 13Gs. Its Clearway Energy stake, held through GIP, is on a 13D. Same parent, two kinds of owner.

Because power companies are regulated, the federal energy regulator ({{FERC}}) must also approve large voting stakes. BlackRock holds its utility shares under a {{blanket authorization}} that assumes they stay passive. In July 2026 consumer groups asked FERC to force BlackRock to separate the passive business from the controlling one.

sections.title: What BlackRock bought when it bought GIP
sections.read: A team and its contracts to manage other people's money — not the assets themselves.
ps: BlackRock completed its purchase of Global Infrastructure Partners on 1 October 2024, paying USD 3bn in cash and about 12 million of its own shares, part of them paid years later against performance targets — {{deferred consideration}}. It then put its own infrastructure businesses under the GIP name.

The data centres and power plants belong to GIP's funds, whose investors ({{limited partner}}s) are pension funds, sovereign funds and insurers. GIP chooses the investments and earns fees. 'BlackRock owns CyrusOne' is shorthand for 'funds managed by BlackRock's GIP co-own CyrusOne'.

That is why BlackRock's infrastructure is counted three ways at once, shown below: what pays a fee now, everything clients have committed, and GIP's own description. The gap between the first two is mostly {{dry powder}} — money promised but not yet invested.

sections.title: Who bought Aligned: three names, two controllers
sections.read: A press release names buyers; a merger-control decision names controllers.
ps: Aligned Data Centers' closing release of 21 July 2026 names 'AIP, MGX, and BlackRock's GIP' as buyers of 100% of the equity, at about USD 40bn of {{enterprise value}}.

A {{consortium}} buys through a shared vehicle, and a shareholders' agreement decides who sets strategy. European merger law asks exactly that. In Case M.12259 the European Commission named two parties acquiring {{joint control}}: Global Infrastructure Management, LLC (ultimately BlackRock) and MGX Fund Management Limited. The AI Infrastructure Partnership was not a notifying party.

AIP itself was launched in September 2024 by BlackRock, GIP, Microsoft and MGX to raise USD 30bn of equity and up to USD 100bn with debt for data centres and their power. NVIDIA and xAI joined in March 2025, and the Kuwait Investment Authority and Temasek became anchors. No first-party source gives its legal form. It works as a pool of money that invests through GIP and MGX, and MGX also invested directly beside it — {{co-investment}}.
For a seller the membership is the point: the tenants' own capital, Microsoft's, NVIDIA's and xAI's, sits among the landlord's owners.

sections.title: What regulators ask a new owner for
sections.read: Every approval can come with conditions, and the conditions reshape the utility's spending.
ps: **{{Section 203}}.** FERC must approve anyone buying control of, or a large voting stake in, a regulated power company. For AES it must also weigh the argument that BlackRock's passive stakes in rival utilities give it 'a novel degree of influence', a phrase from its own April 2025 order.

**State commissions.** Minnesota approved ALLETE's take-private by GIP and CPP Investments in October 2025 with about USD 200m of customer benefits, including a one-year base-rate freeze and USD 50m of rate credits. Ohio's conditions for AES reportedly include no merger-driven rate changes and recusal of directors with data-centre interests.
**{{CFIUS}}.** Screens foreign money for national-security risk; AES's co-underwriters include the Qatar Investment Authority.
**The clock.** A signed deal carries an {{outside date}}, after which either side may walk away. A regulator that orders a hearing can push a deal toward it.

sections.title: Moving a campus off a hyperscaler's balance sheet
sections.read: How an investor can own 80% of a campus it neither designs nor occupies.
ps: Meta announced on 28 July 2026 a roughly USD 14bn, 1 GW data-centre campus in El Paso in which funds managed by BlackRock will own 80% and Meta 20%. Meta contributes about USD 2.3bn of land and work in progress, BlackRock about USD 4.9bn in cash, and a USD 12.5bn debt financing funds much of the rest.

Meta is the only tenant on a four-year lease extendable to twenty years, and gives a {{residual value guarantee}} of about USD 13bn — if the campus is worth less than that when the lease ends, Meta pays the difference. That guarantee is what makes the investor's 80% financeable.
Meta also provides construction management and property management, so the investor owns the asset while the tenant runs the build. For a supplier, the design authority at El Paso is Meta's.

Status matters: Meta's quarterly filing two days after the announcement called it an 'exclusivity agreement' subject to {{definitive agreement}}s, and no closing notice had been found by 26 September 2026.

sections.title: Directory or door: what BlackRock is worth to a seller
sections.read: The honest answer to 'should I call BlackRock?'
sections.intro: Weigh the value of knowing the owner against the fact that the owner does not buy.

adv: **One map, many buyers.** The same GIP funds sit above data-centre landlords, a utility, a renewables sponsor and battery owners.
**Shared policy.** A sponsor's risk and compliance rules can shape what its platforms may buy, so a reference at one platform can travel to another.
**Early signals.** A new take-private or consortium tells a seller which buyer will soon have a new capital plan.
dis: **No purchase order.** BlackRock, Inc. signs none; the platform's engineers do.
**Shared control.** At Aligned, CyrusOne, Coravel and ALLETE a co-owner can block a large contract.
**Moving parts.** Battery platforms whose 2026 releases name no owner may be sold before a supplier relationship pays back.

sections.title: Flashcards
sections.read: Concept recall — none of these asks for a date, a name or a fund size.

cards.q: What does filing a {{Schedule 13G}} rather than a {{Schedule 13D}} tell you about a large shareholder?
cards.a: That it certifies it is passive and will not seek to influence control. A 13D holder can or intends to influence control.

cards.q: Why can an {{index fund}} manager hold 10% of a utility without deciding anything about it?
cards.a: The fund buys whatever is in the index in proportion to its weight. It does not choose the company, seek board seats or direct management, and its filings certify that.

cards.q: A press release names three buyers; a merger-control decision names two parties acquiring {{joint control}}. Which tells you who governs the company?
cards.a: The decision. Control means the power to decide strategy and major contracts, and that is what the regulator examines.

cards.q: What is {{deferred consideration}} for, in the purchase of a management firm?
cards.a: It pays part of the price later and only if targets are met, which keeps the acquired team working to the buyer's plan.

cards.q: Why is infrastructure 'fee-paying AUM' smaller than 'client assets'?
cards.a: Client assets include money committed but not yet invested and co-investment that pays no fee; only invested, fee-bearing capital counts as fee-paying.
Whether a purchase of control, or of a large voting stake, in a regulated power company can proceed — and on what conditions — given its effect on competition, rates and regulation.

cards.q: Why does a {{residual value guarantee}} matter in a sale-and-lease-back campus?
cards.a: It shifts the risk that the campus is worth little at the end of the lease to the tenant, which lets the owner borrow against the asset.

cards.q: An investor owns 20% of a developer through {{preferred equity}}. Does it pass the buying-authority test?
cards.a: No. A minority preferred position pays first and carries protections, but it gives no control over what the developer buys.

items.q: Which BlackRock position gives it a say over a platform's equipment purchases?
c: A 9% index stake filed on a 13G
A controlling stake held through GIP funds
A term loan from its private-credit arm
items.why: Only control — alone or jointly — reaches the board and the management that approve purchases. Passive stakes, loans and MOUs do not.

items.q: A utility take-private has shareholder approval and CFIUS clearance. What can still stop it?
c: Federal energy and state commission approvals, and the outside date
items.why: FERC and each relevant state commission must approve, and if they have not by the {{outside date}} either side may walk away.

items.q: Why was the AI Infrastructure Partnership not a notifying party to the Aligned merger review?
c: It had not yet been formed
It is a pool of capital that invests through GIP and MGX, which were named as acquiring control
It bought a minority stake below the notification threshold
The deal was not reviewed in Europe
items.why: The Commission named the parties acquiring {{joint control}}; AIP's money is deployed through vehicles those parties manage.

items.q: At a campus where an investor owns 80%, the tenant runs construction and gives a residual value guarantee. Whose engineers most likely set the electrical design?
items.why: The tenant manages construction and occupies the whole campus; the investor's role is capital.

items.q: A news report says a buyer is in exclusive talks. How should a dossier record it?
c: As a signed deal awaiting approval
As reported talks that bind no one to buy
items.why: {{Exclusive talks}} commit the seller to negotiate with one party for a time, but no one is bound to buy or sell.

items.q: Why is a manager's infrastructure described by several different AUM numbers?
c: Each counts a different thing: fee-paying capital, committed capital, and the manager's own headline
items.why: Fee-paying AUM excludes committed-but-undeployed money that client assets include; a manager's own figure may use yet another definition.

glossary.d: The Phase F screen for this corpus: does a company, or a platform it controls alone or jointly, sign for batteries, medium-voltage switchgear, generation or solid-state transformers? An investor passes only through a platform it controls.
The US Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period: large acquisitions must be notified to the antitrust agencies and cannot close until the waiting period ends.
